rows.answer_text:

1. Beneficial Owner (BO) Accounts
2. Depository Participants (DP) Related
3. Issuer related
4. Depositories Related

Efforts have been made to include provisions of circulars/communications relevant to each section. However, cross-referencing of circulars/communications among the sections may exist. Users are advised to refer to other sections for compliance to provisions applicable to them.

rows.query: Master circular for ESG rating providers
rows.answer_text: The Master Circular for ESG Rating Providers (ERPs) is a document that provides regulatory guidance for entities engaged in the provision of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) ratings. It is issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) and is amended from time to time to reflect changes in the regulatory framework. The circular lays down the guidelines for the registration, general obligations, manner of inspection, and code of conduct applicable to ESG rating providers. It also specifies the procedural and disclosure requirements for ERPs, aiming to facilitate the industry and other users to have access to all the applicable directions to ERPs at one place. The circular is directed to comply with the conditions laid down in this master circular and to have necessary systems and infrastructure in place for its implementation.

rows.query: Master circular for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs)
rows.answer_text: The Master Circular for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) is a document that consolidates the provisions of all applicable circulars issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for Real Estate Investment Trusts. This circular is designed to provide stakeholders with an access to all the relevant circulars at one place, ensuring transparency and facilitating compliance with regulatory requirements. The circular's provisions are incorporated from the circulars issued till the specified date, which varies depending on the circular. For instance, the circular issued on March 28, 2025, incorporates provisions from May 15, 2024, while the circular issued on August 6, 2024, incorporates provisions from May 15, 2024. This document is essential for the effective regulation of Real Estate Investment Trusts in India.

rows.query: Master circular for portfolio managers
rows.answer_text: The Master Circular for Portfolio Managers, as mentioned in the sources, is a document issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to facilitate the effective regulation of portfolio managers. It includes provisions for effective regulation of Portfolio Managers, including those with assets under management (AUM) of INR 1000 crores or more. The circular also mandates that Portfolio Managers with AUM of INR 1000 crores or more must have an automated system in place with minimal manual intervention to ensure effective funds and security. The circular also rescinds certain circulars issued by SEBI and continues to be in force with respect to other laws. The Master Circular comes into force from the date of its issue.

rows.query: Disclosure of material events including buy back of securities by listed entities
rows.answer_text:
The material events including buyback of securities by listed entities should be disclosed on a quarterly basis in the format specified as part of the Integrated Filing (Governance). The disclosure includes the following information:

a) Number of securities proposed for buyback
b) Number of securities proposed for buyback as a percentage of existing paid-up capital
c) Buyback price
d) Actual securities in number and percentage of existing paid-up capital bought back
e) Pre and post shareholding pattern.

rows.query: Review of the block deal framework
rows.answer_text: The block deal framework has been reviewed to ensure that large trades are executed through a single transaction without placing either the buyer or seller in an advantageous position. The Stock Exchanges are permitted to provide a separate trading window during trading hours between 08:45 AM to 05:00 PM for the Block deal mechanism. Additionally, every trade executed in the block deal window must result in delivery and shall not be squared off or reversed. The framework has been reviewed to rationalise the existing technical glitch framework for stock brokers, addressing the 'technical glitches' in Electronic Trading Systems. The extant technical glitch framework has been rationalised based on the size of the stock brokers and their technology dependency. The framework has been reviewed to rationalise the financial disincentive structure considering the exemptions, type of glitches, major or minor, and the frequency of the occurrences. The extant technical glitch framework has been rationalised to rationalise the financial disincentive structure considering the exemptions, type of glitches

rows.query: Revision of the order-to-trade ratio framework
rows.answer_text: The order-to-trade ratio (OTR) framework is applicable to orders placed in the cash segment and the derivative segment, including orders placed under the liquidity enhancement schemes. However, algorithmic orders placed by Designated Market Makers for market making activity are exempted from the framework for imposing penalties for high OTR. Additionally, the framework requires stock exchanges to ensure the maintenance of orderly trading by putting in place effective economic disincentives with regard to high daily order-to-trade ratios of algorithmic orders by the stock brokers. Furthermore, the framework requires the stock exchanges to monitor the daily order-to-trade ratio and initiate measures to impede any possible instances of order flooding by algos.

rows.query: Framework for intraday position limits monitoring for equity index derivatives
rows.answer_text:
The framework for intraday position limits monitoring for equity index derivatives is as follows:

- **Intraday Monitoring**: In addition to the end-of-day monitoring mechanism, the position limits for equity index derivative contracts will be monitored on an intraday basis starting from April 1, 2025.

- **Position Limit**: The position limit for each entity shall be ₹5,000 crore, which is higher than the ₹1,500 crore limit for end-of-day monitoring.

- **Intraday Monitoring Mechanism**: Stock exchanges shall consider at least 4 position snapshots during the day, with the number of snapshots decided by the respective Stock Exchanges subject to a minimum of 4 snapshots in a day. The snapshots shall be randomly taken during pre-defined time windows.

- **Penalty Structure**: The existing penalty structure for breach of end-of-day position limit will be extended by exchanges for intraday position limit breaches as well.

rows.query: Format of the disclosure document for portfolio managers
rows.answer_text:
The format of the disclosure document for portfolio managers is as follows:

- **"Details of investments in the securities of related parties of the Portfolio Manager":** 
  - **Sr.** - Serial number
  - **Investment Name** - Name of investment
  - **Amount** - Amount of investment
  - **Cost** - Cost of investment
  - **Value** - Value of investment
  - **Percentage of total** - Percentage of total investment
  - **Total AUM** - Total Asset Under Management
  - **Last day of the previous calendar quarter** - Date of last quarter

- **"Details of investments in the securities of associates/related parties of the Portfolio Manager":**
  - **Sr.** - Serial number
  - **Investment Name** - Name of investment
  - **Amount** - Amount of investment
  - **Cost** - Cost of investment
  - **Value** - Value of investment

rows.query: Reclassification of REITs as equity related instruments
rows.answer_text: With a view to facilitate enhanced participation by Mutual Funds and Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs), the SEBI has amended the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, to reclassify Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) as equity-related instruments. This reclassification is effective from January 1, 2026, and impacts investments made by Mutual Funds and SIFs in REITs. Existing investments in REITs held by debt schemes of Mutual Funds and investment strategies of SIFs as on December 31, 2025, are grandfathered, but AMCs are encouraged to divest REITs from respective portfolios of debt schemes considering the market conditions, liquidity, and interest of investors. The reclassification also includes the inclusion of REITs in the list of scrips for the purpose of preparation of financial information under the Real Estate Investment Trust Regulations.

rows.query: How will the day's final stock price be determined instead of the volume-weighted average of the last half hour of trading?
rows.answer_text: The final stock price will be determined based on the Volume Weighted Average Price (VWAP) of the constituents of the underlying index between 4:00 pm and 5:00 pm on the expiry day of the Index options contract. In the absence of trading in any constituent during the last one hour, the stock exchange shall determine an appropriate methodology (in line with the methodology for determining daily closing price) to arrive at an appropriate price of the constituent to be used for determining the index price.

rows.query: If a brokerage's order platform malfunctions during market hours, what must the firm do and are smaller firms exempt?
rows.answer_text:
Based on the available sources, if a brokerage's order platform malfunctions during market hours, the firm must implement various mechanisms to minimize losses, including:

- Implementing suitable clauses in their agreement with software vendors to define liabilities in case of software malfunction
- Considering taking suitable insurance cover to meet probable losses in case of software malfunction

The sources indicate that smaller size stock brokers are excluded from the technical glitch framework, which implies that they are not exempt from the measures described. However, the sources do not explicitly state whether smaller brokers are exempt from the measures described. Therefore, based on the available evidence, it is not clear whether smaller brokers are exempt from the measures described.

rows.query: What are the trading-window rules for executing very large share transactions as a single negotiated trade on the exchange?
rows.answer_text:
The trading-window rules for executing very large share transactions as a single negotiated trade on the exchange are as follows:

- Block deals are defined as large trades executed through a single transaction without placing either the buyer or seller in an advantageous position.
- Stock exchanges may set their trading hours between 08:45 AM to 05:00 PM.
- For block deals, the Stock Exchanges are permitted to provide a separate trading window(s).
- The Block deal framework modification includes the provision that all parties to the trade shall have submitted to the jurisdiction of the court specified by the Byelaws and Regulations of the Exchanges for the purpose of giving effect to the provisions of the Rules, Byelaws, and Regulations of the Exchanges and the circulars issued thereunder.

rows.query: What net and gross futures-equivalent exposure caps apply to index options during the trading day, and how are they monitored?
rows.answer_text:
The net and gross futures-equivalent exposure caps for index options during the trading day are as follows:

- **End of Day**: ₹500 crores net, ₹1,500 crores gross
- **Intraday**: ₹1,000 crores net, ₹2,500 crores gross

These caps are monitored by Stock Exchanges. If the net or gross futures-equivalent exposure exceeds these limits, the Stock Exchanges are required to notify the entities (and their Clearing Members) through whom they clear their derivative trades. This notification is made by the Stock Exchanges by intimating the entities (and their Clearing Members) if the FutEq OI in options on any index is beyond the permissible limit.

rows.query: What new requirements govern the appointment and duties of the MD, CTO and CISO at exchanges, clearing corporations and depositories?
rows.answer_text:
The new requirements include:

- The MD and director(s) of the MIIs are to report to the MD.
- The CTO and CISO are to report to the MD.
- The CISO shall report directly to the MD & CEO of the MII.
- The CISO is expected to work closely with various departments of MIIs, including the Network team, Cyber Security team, and IT team.
- The CISO shall deploy appropriate technology tools of adequate capacity to cater to its requirements.
- The CISO's reporting to the MD & CEO is to be drawn from the Ministry of Electronics and IT Notification No. 6(12)/2017-PDP-CERT-In dated March 14, 2017.
- The CISO's reporting to the MD & CEO is to comply with the "financial disincentive" requirements.

rows.query: What is the tender offer route procedure and timeline for a listed company repurchasing its own shares?
rows.answer_text:
The tender offer route procedure for a listed company to repurchase its own shares involves several steps. Here's a summary of the procedure:

1. **Public Announcement**: The company must publicly announce its intention to repurchase its own shares within 2 working days from the board meeting where the buyback proposal is approved.

2. **Dispatch of Final Letter**: The company must dispatch a final letter to the shareholders within 5 working days from the date of the board meeting. This letter should include details of the buyback proposal, the terms of the offer, the price per share, the number of shares to be repurchased, and the date of the offer.

3. **Opening of Offer**: The offer is kept open for 10 working days from the date of dispatch of the final letter. During this period, the offer is available for inspection by shareholders.

4. **Availability of Material**: Shareholders are given a specific address to obtain the documents for inspection. Shareholders can modify or cancel

rows.query: What disclosures must a listed company make for employee stock option schemes under the share based employee benefits framework?
rows.answer_text:
A listed company must comply with the following requirements for disclosure of Employee Benefit Scheme Documents in terms of Regulation 46(2)(za) of the LODR:

a. The scheme document shall be uploaded on the website of the listed entity after obtaining shareholder approval as required under SEBI (SBEB) Regulations, 2021.

b. The documents uploaded on the website shall mandatorily have minimum information to be disclosed to shareholders as per SEBI (SBEB) Regulations, 2021.

c. The rationale for redacting information from the documents and the justification as to how such redacted information would affect competitive position or reveal commercial secrets of the listed entity shall be placed before the board of directors for consideration and approval.

d. The secretarial compliance report issued by a Peer Reviewed Company Secretary under Regulation 24A(2) of the LODR Regulations shall include a confirmation on compliance with the aforesaid requirements by the listed entity.

rows.query: What are the issuance and listing requirements for municipal bonds issued by urban local bodies?
rows.answer_text:
The issuance and listing requirements for municipal bonds issued by urban local bodies are specified in the Circular No. 66 of the Divisional Council of SEBI. According to the Circular, an issuer desirous of issuing transition bonds shall make the following additional disclosures:

3.1 Disclosure in the offer document for public issues /private placements of such transition bonds:

a. To differentiate transition bonds from other categories of green debt security, the issuer of transition bonds shall use a denotation 'GB-T'. The denotation shall be disclosed in the offer documents on the cover page and in the type of instrument field in the term sheet.

b. Transition Plan, which shall contain the following:

(i) Details of interim targets*/ milestones along with an indicative timeline for achieving the targets.

*interim targets should also reflect the indicative figure regarding how much emissions the issuer is envisaging to reduce.

rows.query: What is the framework for trading electronic gold receipts on stock exchanges?
rows.answer_text: The framework for trading electronic gold receipts (EGR) on stock exchanges in India is structured into three tranches. In tranche 1, physical gold is converted into EGR. In tranche 2, EGR is traded on stock exchanges. In tranche 3, EGR can be converted into physical gold. Additionally, stock exchanges may launch contracts with different denominations for trading and/or conversion of EGR into gold.

rows.query: What are the registration requirements for foreign venture capital investors?
rows.answer_text: The registration requirements for foreign venture capital investors (FVCIs) include obtaining a firm commitment from their investors for a contribution of at least USD 1 million at the time of application. This commitment is necessary for the FVCIs to register with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) as FVCIs. Additionally, FVCIs are required to submit quarterly reports to SEBI in the format specified by the regulations. The regulations also specify that FVCIs must comply with KYC, AML/CFT requirements, and may be excluded from submitting compliance with the Resilience Framework.

rows.query: What does SEBI's February 2024 circular say about the process for returning a draft offer document and resubmitting it?
rows.answer_text:
According to the February 2024 circular (SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/009), the process for returning a draft offer document and resubmitting it involves scrutinizing the document based on broad guidelines. If the document is not compliant with the instructions provided under Schedule VI of the ICDR Regulations and guidelines, it shall be returned to the issuer. Additionally, the circular states that where the draft offer document is returned in terms of these guidelines, there shall be no requirement for payment of any fees on account of resubmission of the draft offer document.

Note: this answer cites circular(s) that are no longer in force — SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/009 has been superseded by SEBI/HO/CFD/PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/0154, HO/49/14/14(2)2026-CFD-POD2/I/4518/2026. Refer to the superseding circular(s) for current requirements.

rows.query: What does SEBI's 2018 master circular for debenture trustees cover?
rows.answer_text:
The 2018 Master Circular for Debenture Trustees (DTs) issued by SEBI covers various aspects of the securities market, including:

1. **Monitoring of Utilization Certificate and Security Cover**: The circular provides guidelines on the monitoring of utilization certificates and security cover, including the type, size, status, and performance of the security.

2. **Periodical Review of Regulatory Compliance**: The circular includes a review of regulatory compliance, periodic assessment of the regulatory framework, and the enforcement of security as per terms of issue/ regulatory guidelines.

3. **Details of Services Provided by Debenture Trustee**: The circular details the services provided by the Debenture Trustee, such as facilitating documentation, exercising due diligence, timely creation of security, ensuring creation of securities by the issuer, holding of security, safe custody of documents, monitoring of payment of interest/redemption of principal, monitoring security cover, other financial covenants, timely and effective resolution of investor complaints, ensuring compliance

rows.query: After a company's share transfer agent finishes processing a share transfer, how and when do they need to tell the depository participant about it?
rows.answer_text: After a company's share transfer agent finishes processing a share transfer, they need to tell the depository participant about it within two hours. If the confirmation is not sent within two hours, the transfer is deemed to have been confirmed. The registrar shall not reject inter-depository transfers except where a Depository does not have adequate balance of securities in its account or there is a mismatch of transfer requests from the Depositories.

rows.query: Are stockbrokers required to keep their clients' money in a separate bank account from their own funds?
rows.answer_text: Yes, stockbrokers are required to keep their clients' money in a separate bank account from their own funds. This obligation is stipulated in the circulars issued by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI). The circulars mandate that every member broker must forthwith pay the money to the current or deposit account at a bank to be kept in the name of the member, with the word "clients" appearing in the account title. This ensures that the broker's own funds and securities are kept separate from those belonging to the clients. The broker may keep one consolidated clients account for all the clients or accounts in the name of each client, as they think fit, provided that when a Member broker receives a cheque or draft representing in part money belonging to the client and in part money due to the Member, they shall pay the whole of such cheque or draft into the clients account and effect subsequent transfer as laid down below in para 23.1.4(b).

rows.query: Does SEBI's cloud computing framework for regulated entities cover a private cloud setup, or is that governed by different rules?
rows.answer_text: Yes, SEBI's cloud computing framework for regulated entities covers a private cloud setup. According to the circular, private cloud deployments are governed by SEBI circulars, guidelines, advisories, etc., issued from time to time. Therefore, private cloud deployments are permitted, but such deployments may not be governed by this cloud framework.

rows.query: If a company doesn't accept the provisional credit rating a rating agency gave it, what extra details must the agency publish about how that rating was arrived at?
rows.answer_text:
If a company doesn't accept the provisional credit rating assigned by a credit rating agency, the agency must publish the following supplementary disclosures on their website:

1. The details of the steps taken for assigning the provisional rating.
2. For instance, in the case of REITs/InvITs, such disclosure should contain the broad details of the assets to be housed under the Trust, the proposed capital structure, etc.

rows.query: Under SEBI's cybersecurity framework, what kind of cyberattack on a regulated entity would count as a 'critical' severity incident?
rows.answer_text: A 'critical' severity incident under SEBI's cybersecurity framework would count as a cyberattack that results in **unauthorized access, denial of service, or disruption** to **critical assets**. Critical assets include **business critical systems**, **internet facing applications/systems**, **systems containing sensitive data**, **sensitive personal data**, **sensitive financial data**, **Personally Identifiable Information (PII)** data, **etc**.

rows.query: If a broker's employee receives some market news or rumor by email, do they need approval before forwarding it to others?
rows.answer_text: Yes, according to the circular, if a broker's employee receives any market-related news or rumor by email, they should forward it only after the same has been seen and approved by the Compliance Officer of the broker. If an employee fails to do so, they shall be deemed to have violated the various provisions contained in the SEBI Act, Rules, or Regulations, and shall be liable for action. The Compliance Officer shall also be held liable for breach of duty in this regard.

rows.query: Are regulated entities required to keep backup 'template' copies of their critical IT systems at a separate location, in case they need to rebuild in an emergency?
rows.answer_text: Yes, regulated entities are required to keep backup 'template' copies of their critical IT systems at a separate location, in case they need to rebuild in an emergency. This is specified in the guidelines for MIIs, which state that MIIs shall maintain regularly updated "gold images" of critical systems for rebuilding purposes. The guidelines also mention maintaining image "templates" that include a preconfigured operating system and associated software applications, which can be quickly deployed to rebuild a system. This requirement is applicable to both on-premise and cloud critical systems.

rows.query: If a broker pays SEBI fees directly via RTGS or NEFT instead of a cheque, does SEBI need to be separately told about that payment?
rows.answer_text: Yes, if a broker pays SEBI fees directly via RTGS or NEFT instead of a cheque, SEBI needs to be separately told about that payment. This is because the Master Circular for Stock Brokers issued on March 06, 2017, states that SEBI has been receiving direct credit of amounts from various intermediaries/other entities. To account for such direct credit in the SEBI account, intermediaries/other entities are required to provide the information as mentioned in Annexure 26 to SEBI once the payment is made. This information should be emailed to the respective department(s) as well as to Treasury & Accounts division at tad@sebi.gov.in.

rows.query: How does a mutual fund investor find out if they have unclaimed money sitting with a fund, and what proof of identity do they need?
rows.answer_text:
A mutual fund investor can find out if they have unclaimed money sitting with a fund by using the following methods:

1. **Website Information**: Mutual Funds are required to provide on their website the list of names and addresses of investors in whose folios there are unclaimed amounts. This information should include the investor's name, address, and the Mutual Fund(s) with which the unclaimed amount lies.

2. **Consolidated List**: AMFI is also required to provide on its website a consolidated list of investors across the Mutual Fund industry, in whose folios there are unclaimed amounts. This list should include the investor's name, address, and the Mutual Fund(s) with which the unclaimed amount lies.

3. **Credentials**: To obtain this information, the investor must provide their appropriate credentials, such as PAN (Permanent Account Number), date of birth, etc., along with adequate security control measures being put in place by the Mutual Fund or AMFI.

rows.query: SEBI made it easier to get 'accredited investor' status recently — what changed to simplify the process?
rows.answer_text:
In recent years, SEBI has simplified the process for obtaining 'accredited investor' status by introducing the concept of 'accredited investor' in the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013. This amendment to the Regulations introduced the framework for accreditation of investors, which has been further simplified by SEBI vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-I/DF9/P/CIR/2021/620 dated August 26, 2021. This circular specifies the modalities for the implementation of the framework for accreditation of investors. Additionally, SEBI vide Circular No. SEBI/HO/AFD/PoD1/CIR/2023/189 dated December 18, 2023, has simplified the requirements for grant of accreditation to investors. These changes aim to provide flexibility and facilitate ease of accreditation of investors.

Note: this answer cites circular(s) that are no longer in force — SEBI/HO/AFD/PoD1/CIR/2023/189 has been superseded by SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD/P/CIR/2025/94, HO/38/12/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4300/2026, HO/19/34/11(6)2025-AFD-POD1/I/12928/2026, SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2024/50, SEBI/HO/AFD-1/AFD-1-PoD/P/CIR/2024/39. Refer to the superseding circular(s) for current requirements.

rows.query: During an IPO, is there a shared dashboard where intermediaries can track UPI mandate approvals and app performance in real time?
rows.answer_text: Yes, during an IPO, there is a shared dashboard where intermediaries can track UPI mandate approvals and app performance in real time. This is facilitated by the use of Issue UPI for payment, where the sponsor bank initiates a mandate request on behalf of the investor to block funds, and the investor accepts the mandate request through their mobile application, associated with UPI ID linked to their bank account. The intermediary then receives the bid details from the stock exchange platform, which includes the UPI ID, and shares this information with the sponsor bank, who initiates the mandate request on behalf of the investor. The investor is able to view the details of the UPI mandate in their UPI application, and authorize the transaction. The sponsor bank for the IPO ensures that the UPI request includes the Invoice in the box parameters as per the NPCI guidelines.

rows.query: If the same outsourcing vendor handles work for several different brokers, what precautions are supposed to stop client data from getting mixed up between them?
rows.answer_text: If the same outsourcing vendor handles work for several different brokers, the intermediary and the third party are expected to take strong safeguards to ensure that there is no co-mingling of information, documents, records, and assets. This involves ensuring that the employees of the third party have limited access to the data handled and only on a "need to know" basis. Additionally, the third party and the intermediary should have adequate checks and balances to ensure that the same. This is to prevent the client data from getting mixed up between the brokers.

rows.query: Can a fund manager place direct market access trades on behalf of an institutional client instead of the client trading themselves?
rows.answer_text: Yes, a fund manager can place direct market access trades on behalf of an institutional client instead of the client trading themselves. This is permitted under the provisions of the circular, which states that a SEBI registered entity shall be permitted to act as an investment manager on behalf of institutional clients. In case the facility of DMA is used by the client through an investment manager, the investment manager may execute the necessary documents on behalf of the client(s).

rows.query: If a foreign investor's trading data is stored in the cloud, does it still need to physically stay within India's legal boundaries?
rows.answer_text: Yes, if a foreign investor's trading data is stored in the cloud, it still needs to physically stay within India's legal boundaries. This is to ensure that the data is not stored on servers outside the legal boundaries of India, which could cause governance issues and limit compliance with various laws related to data protection and cybersecurity. Therefore, the data generated within the legal boundaries of India must remain within India.

rows.query: Can a mutual fund carve out a 'segregated portfolio' just because a bond issuer looks likely to default, or does an actual default have to happen first?
rows.answer_text: Yes, an actual default has to happen first. According to the circular, the AMC may create a segregated portfolio only if the issuer's debt or money market instrument has a downgrade to 'below investment grade' or if there are subsequent downgrades from multiple CRAs. Actual default by the issuer of such instruments is considered a credit event for creating the segregated portfolio.

rows.query: What happens to money that REIT unitholders never claim — does it eventually go to an investor protection fund, and can they still get it back later?
rows.answer_text: Yes, the unclaimed amount paid by the REIT to the unitholder will eventually be transferred to the investor protection fund (IPF) of the Investment Protection Fund (IPF) of the Stock Exchange. The REIT will indemnify the Board against any future dispute that may arise with respect to the unclaimed amount of the unitholder, including on account of a fraudulent claim or misrepresentation by the unitholder. However, this does not preclude the Board from taking any action for the fraud or misrepresentation in this regard.

rows.query: When a listed company evaluates its board chairperson, what extra qualities are they supposed to be assessed on beyond regular director criteria?
rows.answer_text:
When a listed company evaluates its board chairperson, they are supposed to be assessed on the following extra qualities beyond the regular director criteria:

- Effectiveness of leadership and ability to steer the meetings
- Impartiality
- Commitment
- Ability to keep shareholders' interests in mind

These additional criteria are designed to provide a more comprehensive assessment of the chairperson's role and their ability to steer the board effectively.

rows.query: Can an investor get one combined statement showing both their mutual fund holdings and their demat account securities?
rows.answer_text: Yes, as per the Circular ID #3.3, the inclusion of MF and demat holding statements within DigiLocker, the entire financial holdings of individuals can be made available in a single account. This is facilitated by enabling a single consolidated view of all the investments of an investor in Mutual Funds (MF) and securities held in demat form with the Depositories. The Depositories and the Asset Management Companies (AMCs)/ MF-RTAs are required to put in place systems to facilitate generation and dispatch of single Consolidated Account Statements (CAS) for investors having MF investments and holding demat accounts. Additionally, the Circular ID #15.7.3. Dematerialization of existing units held by investor states that the AMCs/ RTAs shall share the requisite information with the Depositories on monthly basis to enable generation of CAS.

rows.query: If most of the money in an AIF scheme comes from investors based in a country that shares a land border with India, is extra background-checking required before investing?
rows.answer_text: Yes, if most of the money in an AIF scheme comes from investors based in a country that shares a land border with India, extra background-checking is required before investing. This is specified in the circular under the section "8.2.1. For every scheme of AIFs where 50 percent or more of the corpus of the scheme is contributed by investors – (a) who are citizens of/are from/are situated in a country which shares land border with India, or, (b) whose beneficial owners, as determined in terms of sub-rule (3) of Rule 9 of the Prevention of Money-laundering (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005, are citizens of/are from/are situated in a country which shares land border with India, necessary due diligence as per the implementation standards formulated by SFA, shall be carried out prior to making any investment."

rows.query: How often does a KYC Registration Agency need to run a penetration test on its systems, and does that change if its systems are classified as sensitive infrastructure?
rows.answer_text: A KYC Registration Agency (KRA) needs to conduct a periodic vulnerability assessment and penetration test (VAPT) on its systems at least once in a financial year. For KRAs, whose systems have been identified as "protected system" by NCIIPC under the Information Technology (IT) Act, 2000, VAPT shall be conducted at least twice in a financial year. This requirement is applicable to all KRAs, regardless of the type of system they manage.

rows.query: If a SEBI-registered intermediary's staff use chat apps or messenger tools for work, do those chat logs need to be preserved as official records?
rows.answer_text: Yes, according to the Master Circular for Credit Rating Agencies issued by SEBI, if a SEBI-registered intermediary's staff use chat apps or messenger tools for work, those chat logs need to be preserved as official records. This is to ensure that any unverified information obtained from client, industry, any trade, or other sources is not circulated without verification. The circular explicitly states that Logs for any usage of such Blogs/Chat forums/Messenger sites (called by any nomenclature) shall be treated as records and the same should be maintained as specified by the respective Regulations which govern the concerned intermediary. This requirement is to prevent the circulation of unauthenticated news by SEBI-registered Market Intermediaries through various modes of communication.

rows.query: Why do mutual fund schemes benchmark their performance against a 'total return index' instead of a plain price index?
rows.answer_text:
Mutual fund schemes benchmark their performance against a 'total return index' instead of a plain price index for the following reasons:

1. **Incorporation of Dividends and Interest**: Total Return indices take into account dividends and interest payments generated from the basket of constituents that make up the index. This ensures that the performance is not only based on capital gains but also on the total return to the investor.

2. **Capital Gains**: Total Return indices include capital gains, which are important for assessing the performance of the scheme's assets over time.

3. **Comparison with Benchmark**: Using a Total Return index allows mutual funds to compare their performance against a benchmark that reflects the true return to the investor, not just the capital gains.

4. **Standardization**: Total Return indices are more standardized and provide a consistent way to compare the performance of different schemes.

rows.query: What kinds of risk limits does a broker have to apply to a client's direct market access orders?
rows.answer_text:
A broker has to apply the following risk limits to a client's direct market access orders:

1. Order quantity/order value limit in terms of price and quantity specified for the client.
2. All position limits specified in the derivatives segment as applicable.
3. Net position that can be outstanding so as to fully cover the risk emanating from the trades with the available margins of the specific client.
4. Appropriate limits for securities which are subject to FII limits as specified by the Reserve Bank of India.

rows.query: What counts as an 'association' between a regulated market intermediary's agents and some other outside person or firm?
rows.answer_text: An association between a regulated market intermediary's agents and another person or firm is considered an association in the nature of a transaction involving money or money's worth, referral of a client, interaction of information technology systems, or any other association of similar nature or character, by any name called. This association is prohibited unless the person is registered with or otherwise permitted by the Board to provide advice or make claims related to securities.

rows.query: If shares held in demat form are pledged as loan collateral and the account holder dies, can the nominee get those shares transferred before the loan is cleared?
rows.answer_text: No, the nominee cannot get those shares transferred before the loan is cleared. According to the Circular, the shares locked-in under this clause may be transferred 'inter-se' among promoters in accordance with the conditions specified under Regulation 22 of the ICDR Regulations. However, the Circular does not specify any specific procedure for transferring shares held in demat form as collateral security for a loan. Therefore, the nominee would need to follow the specific procedure outlined in the ICDR Regulations to transfer the shares held in demat form as collateral security for a loan.

rows.query: If my stockbroker's trading system goes down, is there a backup platform that lets me still close out my open positions?
rows.answer_text: Yes, there is a contingency trading facility provided by Stock Exchanges. This facility allows Stock brokers to square off outstanding open positions for their clients during business disruptions. The Contingency Pool Trading facility operates via the exchange's internal network within its physical premises, where broker allocated dedicated terminals are seamlessly connected to the Stock Exchange trading platform.

rows.query: Under the LODR business-activity disclosure format, what turnover percentage threshold is used to define the 'business activities' that must be listed?
rows.answer_text: The turnover percentage threshold used to define the 'business activities' that must be listed under the LODR business-activity disclosure format is 90%. This is specified in the Master Circular for compliance with the provisions of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, as per Regulation 16. This threshold is used to ensure that a significant portion of the entity's turnover is covered by the disclosure requirements.

rows.answer_text: Yes, under the current master circular for depositories, depository participants are required to send quarterly statements of transactions to clients whose demat accounts have no transactions and no security balances. However, they are exempt from this obligation under certain conditions, including informing the client that they will not receive transaction statements until there are any transactions or security holdings in the demat account.

rows.query: Under the current master circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts, what proportion of units allotted to the sponsor(s) in a preferential issue is locked-in for three years from the date of trading approval?
rows.answer_text: Under the current master circular for Infrastructure Investment Trusts, the units allotted to the sponsor(s) in a preferential issue are locked-in for three years from the date of trading approval. This lock-in period is applicable to units not more than twenty-five percent of the total unit capital of the InvIT.

rows.query: Under the current master circular for depositories, for what two purposes can a client's Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction (DDPI) be utilized by a stock broker or stock broker depository participant?
rows.answer_text:
Under the current master circular for depositories, a client's Demat Debit and Pledge Instruction (DDPI) can be utilized by a stock broker or stock broker depository participant for the following two purposes:

1. To execute delivery obligations prior to the actual transfer of securities.
2. To execute settlement obligations prior to the actual transfer of securities.

rows.query: Under the current master circular for Alternative Investment Funds, in what circumstance is an AIF scheme not required to maintain investors' pro-rata rights in a particular investment?
rows.answer_text: An AIF scheme is not required to maintain investors' pro-rata rights in a particular investment under the current master circular for Alternative Investment Funds if the investor has been excused or excluded from participating in the investment, or if the investor has defaulted on providing their pro-rata contribution for the investment.

rows.query: Under the current master circular for depositories, what type of account must an investor maintain with a depository participant to hold securities in dematerialized form?
rows.answer_text: Under the current master circular for depositories, an investor must maintain a dematerialized account with a depository participant to hold securities in dematerialized form. This is specified in the Master Circular for Depositories, which states that "In case investors desire to convert their existing physical units (represented by SOA) into dematerialized form, mutual funds / AMCs shall take such steps in coordination with RTAs, Depositories and Depository participants (DPs) to facilitate the same."

rows.query: Under the current master circular for Alternative Investment Funds, which industry-endorsed guidelines are used for valuation of investment portfolios not covered under the standard valuation clause?
rows.answer_text: Under the current master circular for Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), the industry-endorsed guidelines used for valuation of investment portfolios not covered under the standard valuation clause are the International Private Equity and Venture Capital Valuation (IPEV) Guidelines. This is specified in the circular under the clause "In terms of Clause 22.1.2 of the Master Circular, valuation of securities which are not covered in para 22.1.1 of the Master Circular, shall be carried out as per valuation guidelines (taking into account recommendations of AIPAC of SEBI), endorsed by any AIF industry association, which in terms of membership represents at least 33% of the number of SEBI registered AIFs."

rows.query: Under the currently applicable norms for processing investor service requests by RTAs, is furnishing of PAN, KYC details and Nomination mandatory for holders of physical securities?
rows.answer_text: Yes, under the currently applicable norms for processing investor service requests by RTAs, furnishing of PAN, KYC details, and Nomination is mandatory for holders of physical securities. This is specified in the Master Circular for Registrars to an Issue and Share Transfer Agents, which states that it is mandatory for all holders of physical securities in listed companies to furnish PAN, Nomination, Contact details, Bank A/c details, and Specimen signature for their corresponding folio numbers.

rows.query: Which SEBI standing committee developed the revised four-level industry classification framework for the Centralized Database of corporate bonds, and is that framework now consolidated within the Master Circular for issue and listing of Non-convertible Securities (as updated July 2023)?
rows.answer_text: The revised four-level industry classification framework for the Centralized Database of corporate bonds was developed by the Market Data Advisory Committee (MDAC), a standing committee constituted by SEBI, comprising of representatives from stock exchanges, depositories, and other market participants. This committee examined existing industry classification structures across sectors and developed a harmonized four-level framework for adoption by all stakeholders and relevant processes/ purposes in the Indian securities market. This framework is now consolidated within the Master Circular for issue and listing of Non-convertible Securities, as updated on July 7, 2023.

rows.query: Per SEBI's November 2022 circular on handling of clients' securities, within how many trading days after pay-out must unpaid securities in the 'client unpaid securities account' be disposed of if the client's funds obligation remains unmet, and does the Master Circular for Depositories (issued December 03, 2024, covering circulars through September 30, 2024) confirm this requirement is incorporated?
rows.answer_text: According to the November 2022 circular issued by SEBI, if the client's funds obligation remains unmet, unpaid securities in the 'client unpaid securities account' must be disposed of within **five trading days** after the pay-out. This requirement is confirmed by the Master Circular for Depositories, which states that the TM/CM must invoke the pledge only against the delivery obligation of the client within five trading days after the pay-out.

rows.query: What regulations govern the nomination and 'choice of nomination' relief measures addressed in SEBI's June 2024 circular, and have those regulatory bases been repealed?
rows.answer_text: The regulations governing the nomination and 'choice of nomination' relief measures addressed in SEBI's June 2024 circular are the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, specifically regulation 36(1)(b) and regulation 44(4) of the SEBI Listing Regulations. This relaxation has been extended till September 30, 2024, for Annual General Meetings (AGMs) and general meetings held in electronic mode.

rows.query: What documents make up the Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC) that stock brokers must give clients free of charge, and is the stock-broker regulation underpinning this MITC requirement still current?
rows.answer_text:
The documents that make up the Most Important Terms and Conditions (MITC) that stock brokers must give clients free of charge include:

1. Account opening form
2. Rights and obligations
3. Risk disclosure documents
4. Guidance note
5. Policies and procedures
6. Tariff sheet

The stock-broker regulation underpinning this MITC requirement is still current as per the latest circular dated May 17, 2023, which prescribes the following uniform documents for formalizing broker-client dealings:

- Account opening form
- Rights and obligations
- Risk disclosure documents
- Guidance note
- Policies and procedures
- Tariff sheet

These documents are required to be provided by the broker to the clients free of charge.

rows.query: Which prior Master Circular did the April 2013 Master Circular for Depositories supersede, and is the depositories regulation it was issued under still in force?
rows.answer_text:
The April 2013 Master Circular for Depositories superseded the previous Master Circular CIR/MRD/DP/13/2013 dated April 15, 2013. The depositories regulation it was issued under, the SEBI (Issue and Listing of Debt Securities) Regulations, 2008, is still in force.

Note: this answer cites circular(s) that are no longer in force — CIR/MRD/DP/13/2013 has been superseded by CIR/MRD/DP/11/2014, SEBI/HO/MRD/DP/CIR/P/2016/134. Refer to the superseding circular(s) for current requirements.

Note: this answer cites circular(s) resting on a repealed regulation — CIR/MRD/DP/13/2013 rests on the Depositories and Participants Regulations, 1996, which has been repealed and replaced by the Depositories and Participants Regulations, 2018; CIR/MRD/DP/11/2014 rests on the Depositories and Participants Regulations, 1996, which has been repealed and replaced by the Depositories and Participants Regulations, 2018. Refer to the current regulation(s) for the governing requirements.

rows.query: Whose bank account may be used for payment of a Mutual Fund investment made in the name of a minor through a guardian, and is the Mutual Funds regulation underpinning this rule still in force?
rows.answer_text: The rule underpinning the payment of a Mutual Fund investment made in the name of a minor through a guardian is outlined in the SEBI Circular No. SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2023/40 dated March 23, 2023. This circular states that payment for investment by any mode shall be accepted from the bank account of the minor, parent or legal guardian of the minor, or from a joint account of the minor with parent or legal guardian. For existing folios, the AMCs shall insist upon a Change of Pay-out Bank mandate before redemption is processed. This rule is still in force as of March 20, 2026.
